environment.description: Same Kubernetes pod but the node runs with a custom AppArmor profile loaded as 'k8s-filewatcher-restrict' applied via pod annotation container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/app=localhost/k8s-filewatcher-restrict. The profile was generated using aa-logprof during a 72-hour training period and uses a deny-by-default posture with explicit path allowances. The profile permits read access ONLY to paths matching /var/app/data/** (non-recursive follow through symlinks is blocked via the 'owner' qualifier combined with deny link subset). Additionally, the profile includes 'deny /etc/** r,' and 'deny /proc/** r,' rules. The pivot_root and mount capabilities are also denied. Note: the profile does NOT use 'audit' mode for the deny rules so violations are silently blocked without logging, which means the application receives EACCES but no audit trail is generated.

config.apparmor_profile_content:
#include <tunables/global>
profile k8s-filewatcher-restrict flags=(attach_disconnected,mediate_deleted) {
  #include <abstractions/base>
  #include <abstractions/nameservice>
  
  /var/app/data/** r,
  owner /var/app/data/** w,
  /tmp/** rw,
  /tmp/ r,
  
  # Network access for WebSocket
  network inet stream,
  network inet6 stream,
  
  # Binary execution
  /usr/local/bin/filewatcher ix,
  
  # Deny sensitive paths - symlink traversal blocked
  deny /etc/** r,
  deny /proc/[0-9]*/environ r,
  deny /proc/[0-9]*/cmdline r,
  deny /root/** rw,
  deny /home/** rw,
  deny /srv/** r,
  
  # Deny link following outside scope
  deny link /var/app/data/** -> /**,
  
  # Deny capabilities that enable escape
  deny capability sys_admin,
  deny capability sys_ptrace,
  deny mount,
  deny pivot_root,
}
config.network: ClusterIP service, no ingress filtering on WebSocket
